items.title: Toronto's New Emergency Backup Goalie Rule Gives Mississauga's Brendan Bonello Another Shot at the NHL
items.summary: Insauga.com profiles Brendan Bonello, a Mississauga product now serving as the Toronto Maple Leafs' emergency backup goaltender after the NHL moved to professionalize the role this season. According to the outlet, Bonello played junior and university hockey along with a brief stint in the ECHL before his playing career wound down, after which he began filling in at Leafs practices and game-day skates whenever an extra netminder was needed. The outlet reports the NHL now requires every team to carry an EBUG on its roster, with goaltenders wearing No. 00 who have 80 games or less of professional experience and haven't played under a standard NHL contract or suited up professionally in the past three seasons. Insauga.com quotes the 27-year-old Bonello, who grew up idolizing former Leafs netminder Ed Belfour, saying he doesn't take the second chance for granted. The outlet also cites Calgary's emergency backup Dusty Nickel, a 35-year-old former Junior A goalie who spent five seasons in the role before recently earning a permanent NHL contract.

items.title: Mississauga Man, 20, Charged After Unprovoked Attack on Yonge Street Demonstrator
items.summary: Toronto police say a Mississauga man has been charged with aggravated assault after a demonstrator was punched repeatedly in the head during a weekend protest in downtown Toronto. According to investigators with the Toronto Police hate crime squad, the victim was walking north on Yonge Street near Grosvenor Street and talking with another demonstrator last Saturday when a man approached from behind and struck them several times without provocation. Police say the victim fell to the ground and suffered injuries to their face and leg. The outlet reports a 20-year-old Mississauga man turned himself in at 52 Division on Monday and was scheduled to appear at the Toronto Regional Bail Centre on Tuesday. Toronto Police say the investigation remains ongoing and are asking anyone with information to call investigators or Crime Stoppers.

items.title: Square One Lands Canada's First SUPER MINISO, a Collector-Focused Take on the Lifestyle Chain
items.summary: Insauga.com reports MINISO opened its first international SUPER MINISO location at Square One Shopping Centre on Oct. 10, giving Canadian shoppers a concept previously only available in China. According to the outlet, the 1,000-square-metre store blends MINISO's usual lifestyle goods, beauty products, fashion accessories and travel items with thousands of products built around licensed entertainment characters. The outlet says the store marks the Canadian debut of the complete NARUTO x MINISO collection and the Stitch Hit Snooze Series, with more merchandise featuring Hello Kitty and Friends, Marvel, Chiikawa, Mofusand and MINISO's own character YOYO planned to follow. Insauga.com reports the SUPER MINISO concept relies on themed displays and dedicated character areas rather than standard shelving, aiming to make browsing itself part of the draw for collectors. The outlet describes the opening as a new chapter for MINISO as it expands beyond its traditional lifestyle-goods format toward character merchandise and themed retail experiences.

items.title: Mississauga Mayoral Candidates Lay Out Plans for Housing, Transit and Property Standards Ahead of Oct. 26 Vote
items.summary: Mississauga.com reports it asked mayoral candidates ahead of the Oct. 26 election how they would address housing affordability, declining MiWay ridership and rising complaints about littering and illegal dumping. According to the outlet, candidates were invited to answer two questions covering property standards enforcement and plans to improve transit access, speed and reliability. The outlet reports one candidate said the city needs more housing ordinary working families can afford, and pointed to faster approvals, purpose-built rental housing and better use of city-owned land as ways to grow the supply. Another response emphasized consistent, citywide enforcement of property standards with faster response times and transparent complaint tracking, rather than making residents repeatedly complain before action is taken. Mississauga.com reports candidates also described wanting MiWay to expand service where demand is demonstrated, improve frequency and connect underserved communities, arguing transit planning should follow where residents actually live and work.

items.title: Port Credit Ratepayer Groups Host Four-Way Mayoral Debate Ahead of Oct. 26 Election
items.summary: Mississauga.com reports the Town of Port Credit Association and the Lakeview Ratepayers' Association are hosting a resident-led mayoral debate on Thursday, Oct. 15, ahead of the city's Oct. 26 municipal election. According to the outlet, the debate will be held at Christ First United Church in Port Credit and is open to residents from across the city. The outlet reports four candidates, Bonnie Crombie, Dipika Damerla, Carolyn Parrish and Alvin Tedjo, are confirmed to participate, with discussion centred on property taxes, citywide intensification, transit and infrastructure. Mississauga.com says candidates will also field questions on provincial decision-making, strong-mayor powers and the city's provincial funding allocations. The outlet reports residents will get a chance to ask their own questions once the formal debate segment wraps up.

items.title: Lakeshore Art Trail Marks 25 Years With Its Biggest Mississauga Show Yet
items.summary: Insauga.com reports the Lakeshore Art Trail is celebrating 25 years with its annual Art Show and Sale this weekend at the Small Arms Inspection Building. According to the outlet, more than 40 artists are exhibiting at what organizers describe as the largest fine art show and sale in Mississauga, with ambitions to eventually match the scale of similar events in Toronto and elsewhere in the GTA. The outlet says the show moved to its current venue in 2022 in partnership with CreativeHub 1352, bringing together 24 artists under one roof for the first time after years of artists displaying work out of studios and local businesses across Clarkson, Port Credit and Lorne Park. Insauga.com reports that first year at the new venue drew more than 2,000 visitors, and organizers now expect attendance to top 4,000 over this year's two-day event. The event remains organized by an artist-run executive committee, the outlet notes.

items.title: Trillium Opens Full-Scale Hospital Room Mockups Ahead of New Mississauga Facility's 2034 Debut
items.summary: Insauga.com reports Trillium Health Partners is giving the public an early look at the future Peter Gilgan Mississauga Hospital through full-scale mockups of hospital rooms at its Trillium HealthWorks Experience Centre. According to the outlet, the new hospital will rise 22 storeys on the same site as the current Mississauga Hospital and is expected to be the largest hospital in Canada when it opens in 2034. The outlet reports the facility will include the Shah Family Hospital for Women and Children, described as the first dedicated medical facility of its kind in Ontario. Insauga.com says Trillium, which also oversees Credit Valley Hospital and the nearby Queensway Health Centre in Etobicoke, is holding open houses on Oct. 20 and Oct. 24 so residents can tour the mockup rooms in person. The experience centre is located just west of Dixie Road at 1225 Dundas St., the outlet reports.

items.title: Mississauga Ward 8 Hopefuls Weigh In on Ridgeway Plaza's Parking and Noise Complaints
items.summary: Mississauga.com reports five candidates running for the Mississauga Ward 8 council seat were asked how they would address ongoing parking, noise and safety concerns at Ridgeway Plaza ahead of the Oct. 26 election. According to the outlet, the plaza has become known for its concentration of Middle Eastern and South Asian restaurants and shops and has grown into a major cultural destination drawing visitors from across North America. The outlet says that growth has also made the plaza a focal point for debates over traffic congestion, parking and noise management. Mississauga.com reports candidates were specifically asked what steps they would take as Ward 8 councillor to manage those issues while still supporting local businesses and surrounding neighbourhoods. The outlet published candidates' emailed responses, edited for length and clarity where necessary.

items.title: Mississauga Seeks Volunteers to Bring Back Dozens of Neighbourhood Ice Rinks This Winter
items.summary: Insauga.com reports the City of Mississauga is calling on volunteers to bring back its Natural Ice Rinks Program for another winter season. According to the outlet, dozens of neighbourhood parks across the city rely on volunteer rink-keepers to build and maintain outdoor ice surfaces once temperatures turn cold enough, typically by late December or January. The city says anyone willing to help must be at least 14 years old and comfortable working outside in winter conditions, often in the evening after dark. Applications are due by Nov. 15, the outlet reports. Unlike larger indoor facilities, insauga.com notes these community rinks exist only because local volunteers show up to care for them through the season, giving residents free spots to skate or play pickup hockey at locations ranging from Celebration Square downtown to parks throughout the city's neighbourhoods. City officials describe the program as a longstanding winter tradition in Mississauga and across Canada.
